bullets: The model picker list was updated to include DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Glyph Cluster, and other new options, while marking several older models as retired.
Beam 1.0 was added to the free model picker, allowing users on free or limited-access tiers to use it with a 256K context window.
YouTube was added to the ad marketplace, but it is restricted to the Earn chat assistant and only supports leaving comments.
The coding assistant now waits up to 20 seconds for code searches to complete, reducing failures on large projects or slow devices.
The assistant now checks if the search tool is missing before suggesting installation, avoiding incorrect advice when the issue is permissions or load.
The command-line tool now reports container, virtualization, and Windows Subsystem for Linux details in its environment information.
The cloud service tracks when a project is too large to save, keeping a note until the issue is resolved for projects over four gigabytes.
The assistant now tailors its post-chat suggestions to chat mode, skipping code assessments and focusing on follow-up questions.
Error messages were updated to point users to the Reconnect folder option when a chat connection is lost or daily limits are reached.
The desktop app now defines a Streak Fire appearance option for accounts that have completed a seven-day usage streak.
The desktop app now supports five new flame-colored themes that unlock permanently at streak lengths of 14, 21, 28, 50, and 100 days.
Web and desktop assistants now follow instructions to build exactly what is requested and limit verification to a single build and server start.
Template instructions now explain how to run command-line tools and browser extensions without forcing them into a website preview.
The assistant now continues interrupted answers instead of failing when a model goes silent for five minutes after producing some output.
The terminal sign-in process now automatically hands off to the local browser on macOS and Windows, removing the need for a manual Connect click.
The terminal now shows only one ad at a time, pausing the input area ad when a promotional card appears after an assistant reply.
Freebucks refund text was updated to explain that users receive back unspent money rather than unused time, with a new daily limit of two hours.
Site deployment and deletion errors now show specific reasons from the hosting service instead of generic failure messages.
The desktop app now tracks whether local MCP tools successfully share their lists with the cloud, showing a connection status for each tool.
The after-action review for coding tasks was extended to 10 minutes and no longer has a strict limit on how much text it can produce.
The turn review system now scans through the entire reply to find its summary section, improving reliability when mixed with code.
The shared cloud contracts now support undoing assistant work to specific messages, monitoring background jobs, and faster theme referrals.
The cloud-only reason was added to the list of why a local run option might be greyed out in the desktop application.
